label: Retrieved Adam Smith’s Theory of Moral Sentiments and impartial spectator against narrow egoism
description: Sen systematically rescued Smith from caricature as a pure laissez-faire egoist, drawing on Smith’s impartial spectator to ground open impartiality in global justice.
dialecticalTension: Integrates Smithian moral sympathy into non-parochial social choice theory.

label: Critiqued Rawlsian transcendental institutionalism in favor of comparative capability realization
description: While deeply indebted to Rawls’s Theory of Justice, Sen argued that seeking a single ideally just institutional arrangement is neither necessary nor sufficient to remedy manifest injustices.
dialecticalTension: Shifts justice theory from ideal social contracts (niti) to realized human capabilities (nyaya).

label: Co-originated the Capabilities Approach before diverging on fixed canonical capability lists
description: Sen’s capability framework formed the foundation for Nussbaum’s Aristotelian-liberal list of ten central human capabilities, while Sen insisted on democratic public deliberation over weights.
dialecticalTension: Balances open-ended public reasoning (Sen) against thick constitutional capability thresholds (Nussbaum).

label: Pioneered capability-based evaluation of substantive freedom over aggregate utility or GDP
description: Sen established that well-being and justice must be measured by what people are genuinely able to do and be—their capabilities and functionings.
dialecticalTension: Refutes utilitarian income metrics and commodity fetishism.
historicalContext: Tanner Lectures (1979) and Development as Freedom (1999).

label: Collaborated on cooperative conflict bargaining models and gender justice metrics
description: Sen’s "cooperative conflict" household model and missing-women analysis informed Agarwal’s empirical theory of intrahousehold bargaining and land rights.
dialecticalTension: Brings formal feminist bargaining theory into development economics.
